learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the nature of psychological stress, its sources, its impact on physical and mental health, and effective coping strategies to build resilience!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Stress is our response to events that disrupt or threaten to disrupt our physical or psychological functioning. It can be positive (Eustress, which motivates us) or negative (Distress, which causes harm).
Stressors are events that cause stress. They include Life Events (major changes like moving or loss), Daily Hassles (traffic, exams), and Traumatic Events (accidents, natural disasters).

Proposed by Hans Selye, the GAS model describes the body's physiological response to stress in three stages: 1. Alarm reaction (fight or flight), 2. Resistance (coping with stressor), 3. Exhaustion (depletion of energy resources).

Coping refers to dynamic efforts to manage stress. Strategies include Problem-focused coping (changing the stressor), Emotion-focused coping (managing emotional reactions), and Task-oriented coping. Life skills like relaxation and diet also build resilience.

fun_activity.title: 📝 The Daily Hassle Log
fun_activity.instructions: Keep a 3-day log of your minor daily hassles (e.g., losing keys, waiting in line). Rate their intensity from 1 to 5. Notice how your body reacts to them, and write down one emotional or problem-focused coping strategy for each!

exam_tips: 📌 Hans Selye's General Adaptation Syndrome (GAS) model stages (Alarm reaction, Resistance, Exhaustion) is a guaranteed 3-mark question.
📌 Distinguish clearly between Eustress (good stress) and Distress (bad stress).
📌 Know the difference between Problem-focused and Emotion-focused coping strategies with examples.
quick_recap: ⭐ Stress is an inevitable part of life, acting as eustress or distress depending on appraisal.
⭐ Selye's GAS model outlines how prolonged physical stress leads to exhaustion.
⭐ Developing healthy coping mechanisms and life skills enhances personal resilience.
